observation.visible_scene: A fixed wide shot of a snow-covered granite valley (El Capitan-like cliff on the left, a rounded peak on the right) under a pink-and-lavender sky, with a foreground of snow-laden conifers and a thick band of mist filling the valley floor between them.
visible_changes: The sky clouds slowly drift and morph across the clip: the blue gap in the upper center changes shape and position, and the pink cloud masses rearrange subtly from first to last frame.

The valley mist/fog swirls and varies in density, alternately thickening and thinning over the mid-ground slopes and the base of the right-hand peak, partially veiling and re-revealing the thin vertical waterfall streak on the right.
The foreground snow-covered trees, the left granite face, and the right peak remain in identical screen positions throughout, indicating a stationary camera with no panning or zooming.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the clip is real-time or a time-lapse of the cloud and fog motion.
The cause of the drifting mist (e.g., wind) and any weather changes before or after this excerpt.
What lies beyond the framing edges and whether the fog eventually clears or rises.
uncertain_details: The exact direction and speed of cloud drift are subtle and hard to pin frame-to-frame.
It is unclear whether the mist is rising vertically or moving horizontally across the valley.
The thin white streak on the right could be a waterfall or simply a mist column; its apparent visibility changes are due to fog movement, not its own motion.
